// version: 1.0. The criterion is the same one Abstractions was held to, and it was set
before it was met: 1.0 is the claim that the shape survived contact with a
SECOND implementation, over real bytes, on the shipped artifact rather than a
reconstruction of it.
DemoViewer.NET re-ran stages 2 and 3 against 0.3.0 -- the release carrying the
prefix ordinal layout (SDK#30) -- and reported on SDK#34:
4,434 ordinal comparisons, 3,688 on present fields, 0 mismatches,
joined by canonical path through the alias tables. 36 of 59 classes
live, 263 entity checks. BindingConformance re-passed over all 59
shipped bindings. ZERO adapter changes -- third consecutive round,
this time across a 4.6x manifest growth (144 -> 674 path entries).
The read this package exists to make correct was measured directly: a marker
AK47 binding reads Clip1 through a base-typed BasePlayerWeapon reference,
using the base's compile-time ordinal 2 against the derived class's binding,
while typeof(AK47) declares no Clip1. That is the base body over the derived
binding -- the exact failure SDK#30 was filed for, now doing the right thing
on live entities 10/10.
WHAT THE EVIDENCE DOES NOT COVER, recorded because 1.0 is a claim and a claim
should state its own edges. 16 of the 59 curated classes never went live on
the reference demo and are therefore unexercised on real bytes:
CWeaponAug, CWeaponCZ75a, CWeaponG3SG1, CWeaponM249,
CWeaponM4A1Silencer, CWeaponMP5SD, CWeaponMag7, CWeaponNegev,
CWeaponP250, CWeaponRevolver, CWeaponSCAR20, CWeaponSG556,
CWeaponSawedoff, CWeaponTaser, CWeaponUMP45, CWeaponUSPSilencer
One demo cannot contain every gun. DemoViewer.NET offered a second-demo sweep
of the tail before this was cut and it was declined, so the residual risk is
taken knowingly rather than overlooked. It is judged small on two grounds:
every one of the 16 is a fieldless marker whose binding is its base's paths
verbatim, byte-identical to markers under the same base that DID sweep clean;
and the prefix law is pinned structurally over all 52 derived wrappers, not
just the live ones.
It is not zero. A marker is only correct if the wire's flattened serializer
for that concrete class carries the base's fields, and the schema's parenting
holds real surprises -- CWeaponMag7 sits under CCSWeaponBaseGun with 11 paths
including m_zoomLevel while the three actual shotguns carry 8, and
CIncendiaryGrenade's parent is CMolotovGrenade rather than CBaseCSGrenade.
Both were found by looking. If one of the 16 turns out to break, it is a
curation or hierarchy fault surfacing after 1.0, and it costs a MAJOR.
1.0 also prices the next change: this package's public surface is outside the
C# surface gate (scripts/sdk_surface.py covers src/CS2OpenDev.Sdk/ only, and
says so in its own limits), so nothing mechanical will catch a removal here.
The 59 base-type edges are pinned as typeof literals in the test suite, which
makes a removal fail compile and an unattended reparent fail an assertion.
That is a narrower net than the siblings have, and the version number is
still doing most of the work.
It does NOT track the family major, and it does not track the abstractions
version either. This regenerates with the schema; the contract does not.
Sharing a number with either would mean one of them moving for a reason that
has nothing to do with it.
// versionHeightOffset: Cancels the commit that changes `version` above, so a MAJOR.MINOR bump cuts a

Safe to introduce with the initial version rather than alongside a bump,

// pathFilters: Its own directory. Unlike the abstractions contract next door, this one SHOULD
move when the schema moves: the wrappers are regenerated from
schema-lens/state.json, so a curation change that adds a field is a real change
to this package's surface and should ship as one.
